title: Present simple: habits and facts
goal: Talk about routines, and never forget the -s
intro: The present simple is for habits, routines, facts and timetables: “I get up at seven”, “Water boils at 100°C”. With he, she and it the verb takes -s: “She works”. This little -s is the most forgotten ending in English, so train your ear for it.

examples: He watches the news every night.

rules.rule: Use it with always, usually, often, sometimes, never, every day.

mistakes.wrong: My father work in a bank.
mistakes.right: My father works in a bank.
She goes to the gym every day.
mistakes.why: she → goes. “Every day” is more natural than “daily” in speech.

mistakes.wrong: I am going to office daily.
mistakes.right: I go to the office every day.
mistakes.why: Habits use the simple present, not -ing.

ex.q: I usually ___ to work by bus.
The shop ___ at ten every morning.
Every Sunday I am playing cricket with my friends.
ex.fixed: Every Sunday I play cricket with my friends.

ex.q: He ___ (watch) a movie every Friday night.

ex.a: My brother never gets up before nine.

ex.q: Say it about your friend: “I play chess every evening.” → “He…”

talk: Describe the daily routine of someone in your family. Use he or she in every sentence and listen for your -s: works, goes, watches.
